item.title: Explicit matrix hitting points for noncommutative algebraic branching programs
item.description: arXiv:2610.37677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-resource black-box identity test for noncommutative algebraic branching programs (ABPs), using ordinary matrix evaluations of the output polynomial. Given an alphabet of size $m\ge1$ and an ABP vertex bound $S\ge1$, we construct one fixed tuple of integer matrices of order $R=(m+2)d(d+1)/2$, where $d=(m+2)S$, with entry bit length $O(d\log(d+1))$. Every nonzero polynomial computed by an ABP with at most $S$ vertices has a nonzero evaluation at this tuple. The construction accesses neither the hidden ABP nor its intermediate gates. A rectangular variant improves the order to $O(m^{3/2}S^2)$. Matrix order, description length, and all returned entries are counted; the total resources are polynomial. The result holds in characteristic zero and in characteristic $p>\binom d2$. The main ingredient is a fixed polynomial frame spanning the joint cyclic module of every matrix tuple from every prescribed vector. A compensating block makes a tagged encoding nilpotent of index at most three, while preserving the original cyclic module. A differential exterior-vector argument then gives a single triangular recurrence with polynomially many outputs. Its shared left-linear circuit is converted into actual integer query matrices by coefficient duality. Two-sided pairing further gives deterministic nonadaptive reconstruction of an equivalent ABP from polynomially many output-only matrix queries. The same frame gives polynomial-cardinality explicit trace separators for simultaneous-conjugation orbit closures, and a fixed nilpotent substitution for bounded-dimensional recognizable series. The latter also tests rational formulas whose given syntax is defined at the scalar origin. We provide complete proofs, construction costs, and exact implementation checks.
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Lu

item.title: Nijenhuis Lie $n$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.37698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a homotopical framework for Nijenhuis operators on semistrict Lie $n$-algebras ($n$-term $L_\infty$-algebras) for every $n \ge 1$ and, more generally, on arbitrary $L_\infty$-algebras. A Nijenhuis operator is defined as a family $N = (N_q)_{q \ge 1}$ of multilinear maps, with $N_1$ linear, realizing an $L_\infty$-morphism from an $N$-twisted copy of the structure to the original one. We prove that this condition is equivalent to the vanishing, at every arity $m$, of the $m$-th Nijenhuis torsion up to a correction term $\Lambda^N_m$ formed by higher-component substitutions, and we provide a closed combinatorial formula for $\Lambda^N_m$ as a sum over set partitions. Along the way, we show that the arity-$k$ Nijenhuis torsion factors canonically as a composite of $k$ commuting elementary slot deformations. The resulting objects form a category $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$; we establish that $\mathbf{NijLie}_m$ embeds as the full subcategory of $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$ on objects concentrated in the bottom $m$ degrees for all $m \le n$. These levels assemble into a tower whose first three stages are classical Nijenhuis Lie algebras, the Nijenhuis Lie $2$-algebras of Das, and the newly introduced Nijenhuis Lie $3$-algebras. We characterize the strict and skeletal objects at every level, introduce $n$-term representations up to homotopy of a Nijenhuis Lie algebra, and prove that the semidirect product construction establishes an equivalence between the category of such representations and split abelian $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$-extensions. Finally, two corrections to published level-three identities are documented, and all component identities up to arity five are verified via computer algebra.
item.dc:creator: Imed Basdouri, Tarek Ben Massoud, Ahmed Zahari

item.title: Finite algebras whose equational probability spectrum contains a big gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.37841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the finite algebras $\mathbf{A}$ for which there is no value $p$ satisfying $\frac{1}{|A|}<p<1$ in the equational probability spectrum of $\mathbf{A}$. We will use the classification to determine which finite algebras have minimal equational probability spectrum. In our final section, we explore the relationship, for finite algebras, between the properties of (i)~having a finite equational probability spectrum and (ii)~being an abelian algebra.
item.dc:creator: Carles Card\'{o}, Keith A. Kearnes, \'{A}gnes Szendrei

item.title: Ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.37848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras, generalizing the well-known binary case. These new structures are defined in terms of nonsymmetric operads. We construct these new operads using ternary operations defined in terms of ternary Rota-Baxter operators. The relations defining these operads lie in the quadratic subspace of the kernel of a rewriting morphism from a free operad to the operad generated by one associative ternary operation and one (or two commuting) unary operators satisfying the ternary Rota-Baxter relation(s). We use computational algebra to compute a basis for the quadratic component of the kernel and thereby obtain the quadratic relations which define these new operads. In the dendriform case, we obtain 3 operations satisfying 10 relations. In the quadri-algebra case, we obtain 9 operations satisfying 50 relations. The latter computations combine modular and rational arithmetic, but we are able to provide certificates of the results which can be verified in characteristic 0.
item.dc:creator: Yu Hin (Gary), Au, Murray R. Bremner

item.title: On the cohomological dimension of Henselian valued fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.37961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(K,v)$ be a Henselian valued field of rank one and of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with value group $\Gamma$ dense in $\mathbb{R}$ and residue field $k$. We compute all the graded pieces of the filtration induced by $v$ on the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ of $K$, in terms of the exterior powers of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space $\Gamma/p\Gamma$ and of the modules of differential forms of $k$. This extends to the non-discrete setting a classical theorem of Kato concerning complete discretely valued fields. We also prove that, when $(K,v)$ is maximally complete, no class escapes this filtration by accumulating at a limit. As an application, we prove the inequality $\dim_p(K)\geq\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\Gamma/p\Gamma)+\dim_p(k)$ between Kato's $p$-dimensions, and we show that it becomes an equality as soon as $(K,v)$ is maximally complete.
item.dc:creator: Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche, Gonzalo Manzano Flores

item.title: Introduction to Separable Simplicial Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.38229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study separable simplicial algebras and Azumaya simplicial algebras.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Huang, Garcia Sun, Eric Zhang, James J. Zhang

item.title: A lattice order on the complex field
item.description: arXiv:2610.38300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Birkhoff and Pierce asked in 1956 whether the field $\mathbb{C}$ of complex numbers admits a lattice order compatible with addition and multiplication. We answer the question affirmatively. Using a valuation with value group $\mathbb{Q}$, we construct a positive cone $P$ by a transfinite recursion of countable ordinal length. At each stage we extend a lattice order on a subspace while preserving its lattice operations in the whole field and maintaining multiplicative closure of the ambient positive cone. These subspaces eventually exhaust $\mathbb{C}$. The construction depends on choices of a valuation extension, compatible rational powers and vector-space bases. The cone $P$ contains $1$ and satisfies $\{x\in P\setminus\{0\}:x^{-1}\in P\}=\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$. The induced order is not total: $i$ is incomparable with $0$. For a chosen transcendental element $t$ and $i^2=-1$, one may prescribe $0\vee i=(t+i)/2$ and $0\vee(-i)=(t-i)/2$. Varying the first extension yields exactly $2^{\mathbf c}$ distinct lattice positive cones on $\mathbb{C}$, where $\mathbf c=|\mathbb{C}|$. The count concerns cones as subsets of $\mathbb{C}$.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhen Bao, Yuehui Zhang

item.title: Maximal regular subsemigroups containing the group of units of transformation semigroups that preserve a uniform equivalence relation with two classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $E$ an equivalence relation on $X$. The semigroup $T_E(X)$ consists of all transformations on $X$ that preserve $E$. Although the collection of all regular elements of $T_E(X)$ is not, in general, a subsemigroup, we investigate maximal regular subsemigroups of $T_E(X)$ containing the group of units $G_E(X)$. We construct two such maximal regular subsemigroups, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$, and show that their maximality holds in full generality for an arbitrary set $X$ and an arbitrary equivalence relation $E$ that is neither the identity relation nor the universal relation on $X$ (whether finite or infinite, uniform or non-uniform). Furthermore, when $X$ is finite and $E$ is a uniform equivalence relation with exactly two classes of cardinality at least $2$, we provide a complete classification by proving that they are the only maximal regular subsemigroups containing $G_E(X)$.
item.dc:creator: Kritsada Sangkhanan

item.title: Eternal Total Positivity and Matrix-Dependent Hadamard Thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.38757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study entrywise powers of totally positive matrices. Our first question is which matrices remain totally positive under every positive Hadamard power. We call them eternally totally positive. Our second question concerns a fixed totally positive matrix: what is the smallest exponent after which all of its entrywise powers are totally positive? We call this number the Hadamard threshold of the matrix. Unlike the usual critical exponent, this threshold depends on the individual matrix. We give a complete characterization in order three, obtain explicit bounds for the transition exponent, and construct symmetric matrices that realize every threshold in $[0,1)$. We also prove the basic transformation rules and continuity of the threshold on the normalized $3\times3$ totally positive cone. For higher orders, we introduce the logarithmic core and use it to expand each minor near the zero exponent. This reduces the $4\times4$ problem to the full determinant and the $3\times3$ submatrices. For symmetric $4\times4$ matrices, we show that a positive-definite logarithmic core makes the full determinant positive for every positive exponent. A two-parameter Hankel family then realizes every threshold in $(1,2)$. Hence the exact range of thresholds in the symmetric order-four case is $[0,1)\cup(1,2)$; neither $1$ nor $2$ is attained. We also give a recursive symmetric ETP criterion in every order and an explicit classification for symmetric Toeplitz matrices of order four. In order five, a certified example exhibits an intermediate-power obstruction in a nonprincipal minor. An explicit order-three condition and a finite critical-point test give a complete order-five test.
item.dc:creator: Shaun M. Fallat, Seyed Mahmoud Manjegani, Mohammadrahim Saeidi Dahaki

item.title: NS-Leibniz bialgebras, the Yang--Baxter equation and relative Rota--Baxter operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.39190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce NS-Leibniz bialgebras and establish their equivalence with matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-Leibniz algebras. In the coboundary case, skew-symmetric solutions of the NS-Leibniz Yang--Baxter equation yield NS-Leibniz bialgebras and correspond to $\mathcal{O}$-operators for the dual regular representation. We study quasi-triangular and factorizable structures, and relate factorizable tensors to quadratic Rota--Baxter NS-Leibniz algebras of any fixed nonzero weight. We also construct compatible bialgebra structures from skew-adjoint Nijenhuis operators commuting with the Rota--Baxter operator.
item.dc:creator: Bei Li, Dingguo Wang

item.title: Averaging Zinbiel bialgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.39220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study averaging Zinbiel bialgebras. We first define representations of averaging Zinbiel algebras and prove a semi-direct product characterization. We then introduce matched pairs and Manin triples of averaging Zinbiel algebras, and characterize averaging Zinbiel bialgebras by these two structures. We show that every averaging Zinbiel algebra induces a pre-Lie algebra, and that every averaging Zinbiel bialgebra induces a pre-Lie bialgebra. We also study coboundary averaging Zinbiel bialgebras and introduce the \(S\) admissible Zinbiel Yang-Baxter equation. Its symmetric solutions give rise to averaging Zinbiel bialgebras. Finally, we investigate averaging operators on quadratic Rota-Baxter Zinbiel algebras and relative Rota-Baxter operators on averaging Zinbiel algebras.
item.dc:creator: Bei Li, Dingguo Wang

item.title: Tensor products of Leibniz bimodules and Grothendieck rings -- an addendum
item.description: arXiv:2610.39342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue our investigation of certain associativity properties (namely, alternativity, power-associativity, or being a Jordan ring) of the non-associative multiplication defined on the Grothendieck group of the category of finite-dimensional Leibniz bimodules which we started in \cite{FW}. Namely, we prove that for every finite-dimensional non-zero Leibniz algebra over an arbitrary field this Grothendieck ring is not power-associative. As a consequence, the Grothendieck ring is also neither alternative nor a Jordan ring. This corrects and generalizes some of our results in the last section of \cite{FW}.
item.dc:creator: J\"org Feldvoss, Chao Ma, Friedrich Wagemann

item.title: Local and 2-local derivations of Block Lie algebras B(q)
item.description: arXiv:2610.39741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every local or 2-local derivation of the Block Lie algebra $\B(q)$, with both basis indices in $\Z$, is a derivation for all $q\in\C$. The proofs use the known description of ordinary derivations, Laurent polynomials, and coefficient comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Jahongir Ruzimboev, Baxtiyor Yusupov

item.title: A note on the ideal lattice of a weighted Leavitt path algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.39842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $L_K(E,w)$ the Leavitt path algebra of a row-finite weighted graph $(E,w)$. Suppose that $L_K(E,w)$ is not isomorphic to an ordinary Leavitt path algebra. We prove that the ideal lattice of every countably generated unital $K$-algebra embeds as a closed interval into the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$. The embedding preserves multiplication of ideals modulo the lower endpoint of the interval. It follows that the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$ is not distributive and that ideal multiplication in $L_K(E,w)$ is not commutative. Moreover, we show that if $(E,w)$ is countable, then $L_K(E,w)$ has exactly $|K|^{\aleph_0}$ ideals, prime ideals, left primitive ideals, and right primitive ideals.
item.dc:creator: Raimund Preusser

item.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.39883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.
item.dc:creator: Junpeng Ren

item.title: Local Derivations and Local Automorphisms of Arbitrary Finite-Dimensional Nilpotent Lie and Leibniz Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.40348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study local derivations and local automorphisms of finite-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie and right Leibniz algebras. We prove that every non-abelian Lie algebra in this class admits both a local derivation which is not a derivation and a local automorphism which is not an automorphism. The constructions use a derivation $D$ satisfying $0\ne D([L,L])\subseteq Z(L)$. For non-abelian right Leibniz algebras, both existence statements hold whenever the dimension is at most seven or the nilpotency class is at most four. We construct an eight-dimensional non-Lie algebra of class five satisfying $\LocDer(A)=\Der(A)$ and $\LocAut(A)=\Aut(A)$. Consequently, eight and five are the least possible dimension and nilpotency class, respectively, for either equality.
item.dc:creator: Khusainboy Atajonov, Abror Khudoyberdiyev, Bakhtiyor Yusupov

item.title: Characteristic identities for orthogonal quantum matrices: examples
item.description: arXiv:2610.37813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we illustrate our recent results regarding structure theory of orthogonal Quantum Matrix algebras \cite{OP-BMW,OP-reciprocal,OP-ortho} using the simplest nontrivial example: the RTT-algebra associated with the canonical orthogonal R-matrix of type $O(3)$ (see, e.g., \cite{FRT}). By introducing a suitable linear order on the set of generators, we obtain a set of quadratic relations defining the algebra. Next, we investigate relations among its higher-degree polynomials. As a result, we verify `in components' the Cayley-Hamilton and the reciprocal relations, obtained earlier with the use of the R-matrix techniques. We explicitly calculate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of quantum matrices and propose a conjecture regarding the form of the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series for the RTT-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Ogievetsky, Pavel Pyatov

item.title: Width and amplitude inequalities over DG-rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.37878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study width over commutative noetherian local differential graded (DG) rings with bounded homology. We establish a derived width formula and prove amplitude inequalities for the derived completion of derived Hom and tensor products. As applications, we obtain Iversen's amplitude inequality and a criterion ensuring that regular sequences on a DG-module are regular on the DG-ring. These applications recover results for DG-modules with finitely generated homology and also hold for derived complete DG-modules. Finally, we characterize Cohen--Macaulay DG-rings by the existence of a bounded derived complete DG-module of finite injective dimension whose amplitude equals that of the DG-ring. This provides a version of Bass' conjecture for derived complete DG-modules.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Ferraro, Zachary Nason

item.title: On End-Semidualizing Modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.37924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and study the notion of End-semidualizing modules which are generalizations of semidualizing modules in the classical sense, and also extend the notion of $S-R$ semidualizing bimodules studied by Holm-White and Wakamatsu. By constrast with these notions, End-semidualizing modules exist abundantly. We characterize these modules by the inclusion of projective and flat modules in their Auslander class, or injective modules in their Bass class, and give criteria for when these Foxby classes satisfy the two-out-of-three property. Over commutative Noetherian rings, we prove base-change and duality results, and characterize local depth inequalities by the inclusion of all modules of finite flat or injective dimension in the corresponding classes.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Ferraro, Justin Lyle

item.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
item.description: arXiv:2610.38760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.
item.dc:creator: Oren Ben-Bassat

item.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.38791v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper \'etale correspondence $\Omega:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(\Omega)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.
item.dc:creator: Guillermo Corti\~nas, Xin Li

item.title: Composition factors and finite representation type
item.description: arXiv:2610.38813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.
item.dc:creator: Liang Chen, Zhenxian Chen, Yongyi Wen, Weiheng Xia

item.title: Number of ends of conjugacy diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2610.38841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a finitely generated group $W_n$ with a conjugacy class such that the conjugacy diagram of this class has exactly $n$ ends. For this class, we compute the quotient spaces of the space of derivations of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[W_n]$ modulo quasi-inner and inner derivations, as well as the corresponding component of the first Hochschild cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Alexey V. Naianzin, Andronick A. Arutyunov

item.title: On strongly FP-injective accessibility and weakly FP-projective periodicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.38859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accessibility results are established for (Cartan-Eilenberg) strongly FP-injective complexes, by first proving the accessibility of Strongly FP-injective modules and then utilizing the pseudopullback theorem. We also prove that every acyclic complex of weakly FP-projective modules has weakly FP-projective cycles over left $<\aleph_m$-coherent rings for a non-negative integer $m$. This is achieved by introducing the cotorsion pairs $\bigl(\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj,\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}inj\bigr)$, cogenerated by all $\aleph_m$-presentable weakly FP-projective modules, and proving that acyclic complexes of modules from the class $\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj$ have weakly FP-projective cycles for every non-negative integer $m$.
item.dc:creator: Ilias Kaperonis, Konstantinos Golfis

item.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given.
item.dc:creator: G. Militaru

item.title: Graded Automorphism of Multiparameter Quantum Matrix Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.39366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the graded automorphism group of the multiparameter quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_{\lambda,\mathbf p}(M_n(\Bbbk))$ over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ for all $n\ge2$ and $\lambda\ne1$. No other restrictions are assumed on $\mathbf p$ or $\lambda$. Every graded automorphism is a torus automorphism, possibly followed by transposition or by simultaneous reversal of the row and column indices. We give the precise parameter conditions for these two involutions. As an application, we also determine the full automorphism group when the multiplicative group generated by the parameters is torsion-free.
item.dc:creator: Hai Jin

item.title: Syzygy-Quiver Formulas and Finitistic Dimensions of Special Biserial Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.39672v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite dimensional algebra over a field $\mathbf{k}$. We introduce the reachable syzygy quiver of $\Lambda$, a directed multigraph whose vertices are the isomorphism classes of indecomposable nonprojective direct summands of iterated syzygies of simple modules, and whose arrows record nonprojective summands of first syzygies. The projective dimension of a vertex is one plus its directed path height, allowing the global and finitistic dimensions of $\Lambda$ to be read off from this height function. This formula holds for every finite dimensional algebra, but its states are arbitrary modules. We show that when the first syzygy of an indecomposable module admits a closed combinatorial description from the bound quiver, this state space reduces to a smaller combinatorial quiver, making the global and finitistic dimensions exact computable invariants. We carry this out in three stages. Over a special biserial algebra, the Liu--Morin closure theorem identifies the reachable syzygy quiver with a string-syzygy quiver whose vertices are string modules. Over a string algebra, this compresses to the relation-chain quiver of Xin and Zhang, recovering their global dimension formula along with a parallel formula for the finitistic dimension. Over an arbitrary biserial algebra, the universal formula holds, but uniform compression to paths or strings is impossible, with the Skowro\'nski--Waschb\"usch algebra providing a witness. Finally, we show two string algebras may share the same Gabriel quiver but have distinct global dimensions, proving the ideal of relations is indispensable for these invariants, and we prove that a pointwise homological reduction to a string algebra on the same quiver preserving the monomials of the relations is impossible.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Sardar

item.title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.39805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schr\"oer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.
item.dc:creator: Mayu Tsukamoto

item.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Del Donno

item.title: Structure of the Cayley-Dickson algebras
item.description: arXiv:2505.11747v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Viewing the Cayley-Dickson process as a graded construction provides a rigorous definition of associativity consisting of three classes, which divides the non-associative parts into four types. These simplify the Moufang loop identities and Malcev's identity and categorise non-associative loops. Analysing the non-associativity structure of sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras uncovers octonion and three quasi-octonion, power-associative subalgebras. Power-associativity is proved to grow by multiples of seven that introduce zero divisors in factors of 84 for all Cayley-Dickson algebras. It is convenient to replace the terminology hypercomplex numbers with ultracomplex numbers to capture the quasi-algebras and since sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras contain quasi-algebras these are ultracomplex. The non-associative types reduce the 84 zero divisors in sedenions via three cycles and four modes down to seven primary zero divisor pairs providing new techniques to analyse the seven quasi-octonions loops in sedenions. The graded notation allows the eight octonion and seven quasi-octonion subalgebras of sedenions to be uniquely derived, up to representation. The zero divisors for split sedenion algebras are analysed and mappings between three of these are provided showing 180 zero divisors and the other split algebra is analogous to sedenions with 84 zero divisors. These split algebras are shown to involve quasi-octonion algebras with mixed signature.
item.dc:creator: G. P. Wilmot

item.title: Automorphisms of Sedenions
item.description: arXiv:2512.07210v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper extends the octonion calibration in Clifford algebra to two related sedenion calibrations. Associative calibrations map quaternion rings in Clifford algebra to those in Cayley-Dickson algebras, with octonions consisting of seven rings and sedenions having 35 rings. A new non-associative calibration is found that is related to the sedenion associative calibration but is invertible, providing a classification of the ideals of Clifford algebra and hence of 8 x 8 matrices.This leads to new subalgebras of Clifford algebras and a thorough analysis of the possible automorphisms of sedenions is applied using the Spin and Pin groups. While the calibrations and automorphisms of octonions have minimal divergence, it is found sedenions extend Lie exceptional algebra, G2, to a Lie algebra of rank 49. This work clarifies and extends Schafer's and Brown's sedenion automorphisms. Brown introduced automorphisms that change the sedenion representation, unlike G2, but Clifford algebra analysis finds there are 92 such pure representations. The non-associative calibrations generate an infinite series of new Clifford subalgebras that match the finite geometry PG(N,2) series, discovered by Gino Fano, and connect the projections of simplices with those from hyper-cubes. The visual representation of sedenions as the PG(3,2) tetrahedron, representing the 15 Fano planes of sedenions, allows the sedenion power-associative loops to be visually distinguished from the octonion loops. The visual representation of sedenions may be important for particle physics and Clifford algebra provides analysis tools for the PG(N,2) series that uncovers the hidden structure of Cayley-Dickson algebras within an associative algebra.
item.dc:creator: G. P. Wilmot

item.title: Unitary-Invariant Decomposition of Reducible Total Least Squares Core Problems
item.description: arXiv:2605.08091v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The analysis of a total least squares problem can be reduced to that of an associated core problem, which typically has lower dimension and improved solubility properties. Nevertheless, even a core problem may remain reducible, admitting further decomposition into irreducible component sub- problems with simpler structure and better analytical properties. We seek the finest decomposition under unitary transformations over C; for real data this decomposition can be strictly finer than the finest one under real orthogonal transformations. We split the data matrix into row blocks associated with the singular subspaces of the system matrix and consider the graph whose ver- tices are the blocks and whose edges correspond to nonzero cross-products. After preliminary splittings that make every nonzero cross-product a scalar multiple of a unitary matrix, we show that the components can be obtained directly from these blocks if and only if the covariance matrices along all cycles of the graph are scalar matrices. Otherwise, there is a chordless cycle whose covariance matrix is not a scalar matrix, and splitting the blocks on this cy- cle along the eigenspaces of the covariance matrix removes the obstruction without changing the decomposition. Based on these results, we propose a recursive strategy that finds all irreducible components over the complex field. The strategy is exact and theoretical rather than an efficient numerical algo- rithm; a small floating-point computation illustrates it. The results depend only on the core problem and therefore apply to general linear approximation problems AX B.
item.dc:creator: Sijia Yu, Bruno Carpentieri, Yan-Fei Jing

item.title: Expander Evolution Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2605.12672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce \emph{expander evolution algebras} (EEAs), a class of nonassociative algebras defined over an arbitrary field $\K$ in which the underlying undirected loopless graph of the algebra -- in the sense of Kowalski -- is an expander graph in the classical sense of Cheeger. Starting from the formal graph definition of Kowalski and the algebraic framework of Tian, we establish a dictionary between combinatorial expansion and algebraic structure: the Cheeger constant of the associated graph governs connectivity, the subalgebra lattice, the growth of the evolution sequence, and -- over $\R$ and $\C$ -- the spectral gap of the evolution operator. Over a general field $\K$ we prove that EEAs are always connected and simple (as evolution algebras), carry no proper large evolution subalgebras, and that every generator of a \emph{symmetric} EEA is algebraically persistent. Over $\C$ we obtain the sharp Alon--Boppana lower bound for the second eigenvalue of the evolution operator, leading to the definition of \emph{Ramanujan evolution algebras} as optimal expanders. We also construct families of EEAs from Cayley graphs of finite groups. We close with open problems.
item.dc:creator: Piero Giacomelli

item.title: A further study of quandles and quandle rings
item.description: arXiv:2608.09149v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate core quandles and idempotents in quandle rings of core quandles. We answer several questions on the rank of core quandles and nontrivial idempotents in quandle rings. We also present solutions to two questions raised in a recent paper about non-trivial idempotents in quandle rings $\mathbb{Z}[R_5]$ and $\mathbb{Z}[C_5]$, where $\mathbb{Z}$, $R_5$ and $C_5$ are the ring of integers, the dihedral quandle of order 5, and the commutative quandle of order 5, respectively. We then study units in extended quandle rings of a trivial quandle and the Joyce quandle, and nilpotent elements in extended quandles rings of a trivial quandle, where the ground ring is an integral domain. As a consequence, we show that the quandle ring and the extended quandle ring of a trivial quandle are not nil clean rings. We also explore prime rings and semi-prime rings among quandle rings. We introduce zero-divisor graphs of quandle rings and find an intriguing mirror symmetry among the in-degree and out-degree of the vertices. Moreover, we find a bivariate polynomial in the ring $(\mathbb{Z}_{2n+1}[Q])[X,Y]$ that determines the commutative quandle of order $2n+1$, where $2n+1$ is prime.
item.dc:creator: Gregory Churchill, Indu Rasika Churchill, Neranga Fernando, Bhitali Kousik

item.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
item.description: arXiv:2609.11588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2$ is invertible requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $\pi\colon S \to R$ with $\pi(1) = 1$. In particular, over $\mathbb{R}$ and every finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ of odd characteristic, a quadratic field extension contains a square root of every possible doubling parameter, so the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over these fields, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over them is at most $(9n-21)2^n+28$ when $n\ge2$. When the top doubling parameter is a non-square, as in the standard real tower, the bound is $(9n-15)2^{n-1}+10$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. When $R=\mathbb{R}$ with every doubling parameter equal to $-1$, the real quasilinear schedule uses fewer total arithmetic operations than both direct multiplication and a uniform algorithm of Cariow-Cariowa for $n\ge4$. An implementation for the standard real tower is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$, for both single and batched products, and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Lemley

item.title: Local wild mapping class groups and cabled braids
item.description: arXiv:2204.08188v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We will define and study some generalisations of pure $\mathfrak{g}$-braid groups that occur in the theory of connections on curves, for any complex reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. They make up local pieces of the wild mapping class groups, which are fundamental groups of (universal) deformations of wild Riemann surfaces, underlying the braiding of Stokes data and generalising the usual mapping class groups. We will establish a general product decomposition for the local wild mapping class groups, and in many cases define a fission tree controlling this decomposition. Further in type A we will show one obtains cabled versions of braid groups, related to braid operads.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot, Gabriele Rembado, Matteo Tamiozzo

item.title: The $q$-deformed random-to-random family in the Hecke algebra
item.description: arXiv:2503.17580v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalize Reiner--Saliola--Welker's well-known but mysterious family of *$k$-random-to-random shuffles* from Markov chains on symmetric groups to Markov chains on Type-$A$ Iwahori--Hecke algebras. We prove that these operators pairwise commute, and that their eigenvalues are polynomials in $q$ with non-negative integer coefficients; we express these eigenvalues in a closed form as certain symmetric function evaluations (which is new even for $q=1$). We show that these operators are simultaneously diagonalizable for almost all $q$, and combinatorially express the dimension of the subalgebra they generate. Our work generalizes and extends work of Reiner--Saliola--Welker and Lafreni\`ere for the symmetric group, and simplifies all known proofs in this case.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Brauner, Patricia Commins, Darij Grinberg, Franco Saliola

item.title: The asymptotic size of finite irreducible semigroups of rational matrices
item.description: arXiv:2601.01236v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we investigate the maximum size of finite semigroups of rational $n \times n$ matrices, with the goal of shedding more light on their structure. Such semigroups provide a rich generalisation of transition monoids of unambiguous (and, in particular, deterministic) finite automata. While in general such semigroups can be arbitrarily large in terms of $n$, a classical result of Sch\"utzenberger from 1962 implies an upper bound of $2^{O(n^2 \log n)}$ for irreducible semigroups. A semigroup of rational matrices is called irreducible if the only subspaces of $\mathbb{Q}^n$ that are invariant for all matrices in the semigroup are $\mathbb{Q}^n$ and the subspace consisting only of the zero vector. Irreducible matrix semigroups can be viewed as the building blocks of general matrix semigroups, and as such play an important role in mathematics and computer science. From the point of view of automata theory, they can be seen as a generalisation of strongly connected weighted automata. Using a very different technique from that of Sch\"utzenberger, we improve the upper bound on the cardinality to $3^{n^2}$. This is the main result of the paper. The bound is in some sense tight, as we show that there exists, for every $n$, a finite irreducible semigroup with $3^{\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor}$ rational matrices. Our main result also leads to an improvement of a bound, due to Almeida and Steinberg, on the mortality threshold of finite semigroups of rational matrices. The mortality threshold is a number $\ell$ such that if the zero matrix is in the semigroup, then the zero matrix can be written as a product of at most $\ell$ matrices from any subset that generates the semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Kiefer, Andrew Ryzhikov

item.title: A Hopf algebra on permutations with a coupling product
item.description: arXiv:2607.23345v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a coupling product and a draw coproduct on permutations and show that they define a graded, connected, cocommutative, free Hopf algebra $\mathbb{KS}$. In characteristic zero, this implies that $\mathbb{KS}$ is isomorphic to a certain cocommutative Hopf algebra associated with the dual of the coradical filtration of the Malvenuto--Reutenauer Hopf algebra on permutations. The coupling product and draw coproduct are permutation analogues of the product and coproduct on the monomial basis of symmetric functions; therefore, we can say that our presentation is a monomial basis for $\mathbb{KS}$.
item.dc:creator: Huilan Li, Yishuo Yang, Nantel Bergeron

item.title: Hyperstructures as complete atomic Boolean algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.25165v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that several categories of hyperstructures, including the mosaics of Nakamura and Reyes and the hypergroups of Marty, are realizable as categories of objects with extra structure within the category of complete atomic Boolean algebras (CABAs) and atom-preserving morphisms.
item.dc:creator: Ariel E. Rosenfield

item.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
item.description: arXiv:2610.14100v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $\Lambda_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partial\Lambda_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question was left open in the previous versions; it has since been settled, $\Lambda_4=S_4$, by a computer-assisted proof of L. Marshall, after an earlier claim by D.Z. Liu, who also proved that $\Lambda_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $\Lambda_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Chebotarev
